fields.title: Absolute Surrender
fields.description: Andrew Murray’s addresses on the one thing God asks and Himself supplies — a life wholly given up to Him. From the title address on absolute surrender, through the fruit of the Spirit, Peter’s repentance, and “O wretched man that I am!”, to being kept by the power of God, Murray presses that what is impossible with man is possible with God.

And the king of Israel answered and said, My lord, O king, according to thy saying, I am thine and all that I have” (1 Ki. 20:1-4).

What Ben-hadad demanded was absolute surrender, and what Ahab gave was exactly what was demanded — absolute surrender. I want to take these words, “My lord, O king, according to thy saying, I am thine, and all that I have,” as the words of absolute surrender with which every child of God ought to give himself up to his Father. We have heard it before, but we need to hear it very clearly: the condition of God’s blessing is the absolute surrender of everything into His hands. Praise God! If our hearts are willing for that, there is no limit to what God will do for us, or to the blessing He will pour out.

Absolute surrender — let me tell you where I found those words. I had often used them myself, and you have heard them countless times. But once, in Scotland, I was with a group of people talking about the condition of Christ’s Church and about what the Church and believers most need. Among us was a godly man who does a great deal of work training Christian workers. I asked him what he would say the Church’s great need was, and what message ought to be preached. He answered very quietly, simply and firmly:

“Absolute surrender to God is the one thing.”

The words struck me as they never had before. The man went on to explain that among the workers he deals with, he finds that if they are sound on that point, even if they are slow, they are willing to be taught and helped, and they always improve. Others, who are not sound there, very often fall back and leave the work. The condition for receiving God’s full blessing is absolute surrender to Him.

So now, by God’s grace, I want to give you this message: your God in heaven answers the prayers you have offered for blessing on yourselves and on those around you with this one demand — Are you willing to surrender yourselves absolutely into His hands? What will our answer be? God knows there are hundreds of hearts that have said yes, and hundreds more that long to say it but hardly dare. And there are hearts that have said it, yet have failed miserably, and now feel condemned because they never found the secret of the power to live that life. May God have a word for every one of them!

Let me say, first of all, that God demands it of us.

God Expects Your Surrender

Yes, this demand is rooted in the very nature of God. God cannot do otherwise. Who is God? He is the Fountain of life, the only Source of existence and power and goodness; in the whole universe there is nothing good except what God works. God created the sun and the moon and the stars, the flowers and the trees and the grass — and are they not all absolutely surrendered to God? Do they not let God work in them exactly as He pleases? When God clothes the lily in its beauty, is it not yielded up, surrendered, handed over to God as He works that beauty in it? And God’s redeemed children — oh, can you imagine that God can do His work in them if only half of them, or some part of them, is surrendered? God cannot do it. God is life and love and blessing and power and infinite beauty, and He delights to give Himself to every child who is ready to receive Him. But ah! this one thing, the lack of absolute surrender, is exactly what holds God back. And now He comes, and as God He demands it.

You know from everyday life what absolute surrender is. You know that everything has to be given up to its own particular purpose and use. I have a pen in my pocket, and that pen is absolutely surrendered to the one work of writing. And if I am to write properly with it, it must be absolutely surrendered to my hand. If someone else holds part of it, I cannot write properly. This coat is entirely given up to me, to cover my body. This building is entirely given up to worship. So do you really expect God to do His work in your immortal being, in the divine nature you received when you were born again, every day and every hour, unless you are entirely given up to Him? He cannot. Solomon’s Temple was absolutely surrendered to God when it was dedicated to Him. And each one of us is a temple of God, in which God will live and work mightily on one condition — absolute surrender to Him. God demands it, God is worthy of it, and without it God cannot do His blessed work in us.

God not only demands it — God will bring it about Himself.

God Accomplishes Your Surrender

I am sure many hearts are saying, “Ah, but absolute surrender means so much!” Someone says, “Oh, I have been through so much trial and suffering, and there is still so much of the self-life left in me. I dare not face giving it all up, because I know it will bring so much trouble and pain.”

How sad, how sad, that God’s children think of Him like this — such cruel thoughts! Oh, I have a message for you, fearful and anxious one. God does not ask you to make this perfect surrender in your own strength, or by the power of your own will. God is willing to work it in you. Don’t we read, “It is God that worketh in us, both to will and to do of his good pleasure” (Phil. 2:13)? That is what we should be seeking: to fall on our faces before God until our hearts learn to believe that the everlasting God Himself will come in to throw out what is wrong, to conquer what is evil, and to work what pleases Him in His blessed sight. God Himself will work it in you.

Look at the men of the Old Testament — Abraham, for example. Do you think it was by chance that God found that man, the father of the faithful and the Friend of God? Do you think it was Abraham himself, apart from God, who had such faith and obedience and devotion? You know it was not. God raised him up and prepared him as an instrument for His glory.

Did not God say to Pharaoh, “For this cause have I raised thee up, for to show in thee my power” (Ex. 9:16)?

And if God said that of Pharaoh, will He not say it far more of every one of His children?

Oh, I want to encourage you, and I want you to throw away every fear. Come with that weak desire you have. Perhaps there is a fear in you that says, “Oh, my desire isn’t strong enough. I’m not willing for everything that might come. I don’t feel bold enough to say I can overcome everything.” If so, I beg you, learn to know your God and trust Him now. Say, “My God, I am willing for You to make me willing.” If anything is holding you back, or if there is some sacrifice you are afraid to make, come to God now and find out how gracious your God is. Do not be afraid that He will demand from you what He will not give you.

God comes and offers to work this absolute surrender in you. All the searching and hungering and longing in your heart — I tell you, they are the pull of the divine magnet, Christ Jesus. He lived a life of absolute surrender. He has taken hold of you; He is living in your heart by His Holy Spirit. You have hindered Him, terribly and again and again, but He longs to help you lay hold of Him completely. And He comes now and draws you by His message and His words. Won’t you come and trust God to work in you that absolute surrender to Himself? Yes, blessed be God, He can do it, and He will.

God not only demands it and works it — God accepts it when we bring it to Him.

God Accepts Your Surrender

God works it in the secret places of our heart. By the hidden power of His Holy Spirit, God urges us to come and say it out loud, and we have to bring that absolute surrender and give it to Him. But remember: when you come and bring God that absolute surrender, it may seem — as far as your feelings or your awareness go — very imperfect. You may doubt and hesitate and ask,

“Is it really absolute?”

But oh, remember that there was once a man to whom Christ said,

“If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth” (Mark 9:23).

His heart was afraid, and he cried out,

“Lord, I believe, help thou mine unbelief” (Mark 9:24).

That was a faith that triumphed over the devil, and the evil spirit was cast out. And if you come and say, “Lord, I give myself in absolute surrender to my God” — even with a trembling heart, even while you are aware that “I don’t feel the power, I don’t feel the determination, I don’t feel the assurance” — it will succeed. Don’t be afraid. Come just as you are, and even while you are trembling, the power of the Holy Spirit will work.

Have you never yet learned the lesson that the Holy Spirit works with mighty power while, on the human side, everything looks weak? Look at the Lord Jesus Christ in Gethsemane. We read that He offered Himself as a sacrifice to God “through the eternal Spirit” (Heb. 9:14). The Almighty Spirit of God was enabling Him to do it. And yet what agony and fear and overwhelming sorrow came over Him, and how He prayed! Outwardly you can see no sign of the Spirit’s mighty power, but the Spirit of God was there. In the same way, while you are weak and struggling and trembling, do not be afraid. Have faith in the hidden work of God’s Spirit, and give yourself up.

And when you do give yourself up in absolute surrender, do it believing that God accepts it now. That is the great point, and it is the very thing we so often miss: that believers should be taken up with God Himself in this matter of surrender. I beg you, be taken up with God. Every one of us wants help, so that in our daily life God will be clearer to us, will have His rightful place, and will be “all in all.” And if we are to have that throughout our lives, let us begin now: let us look away from ourselves and look up to God. Let each of us believe it. Here I am, a poor worm on earth, a trembling child of God, full of failure and sin and fear. I bow here, and no one knows what is passing through my heart, and in simplicity I say, “O God, I accept Your terms. I have pleaded for blessing on myself and others; I have accepted Your terms of absolute surrender.” While your heart says that in deep silence, remember that God is present and takes note of it and writes it down in His book. God is present, and at that very moment He takes possession of you. You may not feel it, you may not be aware of it, but God takes possession if you will trust Him.

God not only demands it, and works it, and accepts it when I bring it — God keeps it.

God Maintains Your Surrender

This is the great difficulty for many. People say, “I have often been stirred at a meeting or a convention, and I have consecrated myself to God, but it passed away. It may last a week or a month, but then it fades, and after a while it is all gone.”

But listen! That happens because you do not believe what I am now going to tell you and remind you of. When God has begun the work of absolute surrender in you, and when God has accepted your surrender, He considers Himself bound to look after it and to keep it. Will you believe that?

In this matter of surrender there are two parties: God and I — I a worm, God the everlasting and almighty Jehovah. Worm, will you be afraid to trust yourself to this mighty God now? God is willing. Don’t you believe that He can keep you continually, day by day and moment by moment?

Moment by moment I’m kept in His love;

Moment by moment I’ve life from above.

If God lets the sun shine on you moment by moment, without a break, will He not let His life shine on you every moment? Then why have you not experienced it? Because you have not trusted God for it, and you do not surrender yourself absolutely to God in that trust.

A life of absolute surrender has its difficulties. I don’t deny that. In fact it has something far greater than difficulties: it is a life that is absolutely impossible for human beings. But by the grace of God, by the power of God, by the power of the Holy Spirit living in us, it is the life we were destined for, and a life that is possible for us — praise God! Let us believe that God will keep it going.

Some of you have read the words of that aged saint who, on his ninetieth birthday, spoke of all God’s goodness to him — I mean George Müller. What did he say was the secret of his happiness, and of all the blessing God had given him? He said he believed there were two reasons. The first was that, by grace, he had been enabled to keep a good conscience before God day by day. The second was that he loved God’s Word. Ah, yes — a good conscience, which means complete obedience to God day by day, and daily fellowship with God in His Word and in prayer: that is a life of absolute surrender.

Such a life has two sides. On one side, it is absolute surrender to do what God wants you to do. On the other side, it is surrender to let God do what He wants to do.

First, to do what God wants you to do.

Give yourselves up absolutely to the will of God. You know something of that will — not enough, and nowhere near all of it. But say absolutely to the Lord God, “By Your grace I want to do Your will in everything, every moment of every day.” Say, “Lord God, let there be not a word on my tongue except for Your glory, not a stirring of my temper except for Your glory, not a feeling of love or hate in my heart except for Your glory and according to Your blessed will.”

Someone asks, “Do you really think that’s possible?”

I ask: What has God promised you, and what can God do to fill a vessel that is absolutely surrendered to Him? Oh, God wants to bless you beyond anything you expect. From the beginning, ear hath not heard, neither hath the eye seen, what God hath prepared for them that wait for Him (1 Cor. 2:9). God has prepared unheard-of things, blessings far more wonderful than you can imagine, mightier than you can conceive. They are divine blessings. Oh, say now:

“I give myself absolutely to God, to His will, to do only what God wants.”

It is God who will enable you to carry out that surrender.

And on the other side, come and say, “I give myself absolutely to God, to let Him work in me to will and to do of His good pleasure, as He has promised to do.”

Yes, the living God wants to work in His children in a way we cannot understand, but which God’s Word has revealed — and He wants to work in us every moment of the day. God is willing to sustain our life. Only let our absolute surrender be a simple, childlike and unlimited trust.

God Blesses When You Surrender

This absolute surrender to God will bring wonderful blessing.

What Ahab said to his enemy, King Ben-hadad — “My lord, O king, according to thy word I am thine, and all that I have” — shall we not say that to our God and loving Father? If we do say it, God’s blessing will come on us. God wants us to be separate from the world; we are called to come out from the world that hates God. Come out for God, and say, “Lord, anything for You.” If you say that prayerfully, and speak it into God’s ear, He will accept it, and He will teach you what it means.

I say it again: God will bless you. You have been praying for blessing. But remember, there must be absolute surrender. You see it at every tea table. Why is tea poured into that cup? Because it is empty and set aside for the tea. But put ink or vinegar or wine in it, and will anyone pour tea into it? And can God fill you, can God bless you, if you are not absolutely surrendered to Him? He cannot. Let us believe that God has wonderful blessings for us, if only we will stand up for God and say — with a trembling will, perhaps, but with a believing heart:

“O God, I accept Your demands. I am Yours, and all that I have. Absolute surrender is what my soul gives You, by divine grace.”

You may not have the strong, clear sense of deliverance you would like. But humble yourselves in His sight, and admit that you have grieved the Holy Spirit by your self-will, self-confidence and self-effort. Bow humbly before Him as you confess it, and ask Him to break your heart and bring you down into the dust before Him. Then, as you bow before Him, simply accept God’s teaching that in your flesh “there dwelleth no good thing” (Rom. 7:18), and that nothing will help you except another life coming in. You must deny self once and for all. Denying self must be the power of your life every moment, and then Christ will come in and take possession of you.

When was Peter set free? When did the change take place? The change began when Peter wept; then the Holy Spirit came down and filled his heart.

God the Father loves to give us the power of the Spirit. We have the Spirit of God living within us. We come to God acknowledging that and praising Him for it, and yet confessing how we have grieved the Spirit. Then we bow our knees to the Father and ask Him to strengthen us with all might by the Spirit in the inner man, and to fill us with His mighty power. And as the Spirit reveals Christ to us, Christ comes to live in our hearts for ever, and the self-life is thrown out.

Let us bow before God in humility, and in that humility confess before Him the condition of the whole Church. No words can describe the sad state of the Church of Christ on earth. I wish I had words to express what I sometimes feel about it. Just think of the Christians around you. I am not speaking of Christians in name only, or of those who merely profess faith. I am speaking of hundreds and thousands of honest, earnest Christians who are not living a life in the power of God or for His glory. There is so little power, so little devotion or consecration to God, so little grasp of the truth that a Christian is a person utterly surrendered to God’s will! Oh, we need to confess the sins of God’s people around us and to humble ourselves. We are members of that sickly body, and the body’s sickness will hold us back and break us down — unless we come to God and, through confession, separate ourselves from any share in worldliness and in coldness toward one another; unless we give ourselves up to be entirely and wholly God’s.

How much Christian work is being done in the spirit of the flesh and in the power of self! How much work goes on day after day in which human energy — our own will and our own ideas about the work — is constantly on display, and in which there is very little waiting on God and on the power of the Holy Spirit! Let us confess it. But as we confess the state of the Church, and the weakness and sinfulness of so much of our work for God, let us come back to ourselves. Who here truly longs to be set free from the power of the self-life? Who truly admits that it is the power of self and the flesh, and is willing to throw it all at the feet of Christ? There is deliverance.

I heard of someone who had been an earnest Christian, and who spoke of the “cruel” idea of separation and death. But you don’t think that, do you? What are we to think of separation and death? This: death was Christ’s path to glory. For the joy set before Him He endured the cross. The cross was the birthplace of His everlasting glory. Do you love Christ? Do you long to be in Christ, and yet not be like Him? Let death be the most desirable thing on earth to you — death to self, and fellowship with Christ. Separation — do you think it hard to be called to be completely free from the world, and through that separation to be united to God and His love, and to be made ready to live and walk with God every day? Surely each of us ought to say:

“Anything that brings me to separation, to death, for a life of full fellowship with God and Christ.”

Come and lay this self-life and flesh-life at the feet of Jesus. Then trust Him. Don’t wear yourselves out trying to understand everything about it. Come in living faith that Christ will come into you with the power of His death and the power of His life. Then the Holy Spirit will bring the whole Christ — Christ crucified and risen and living in glory — into your heart.
